diagnoses.summary: PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with both T2 and SPE violations, and the highest rule-based evidence points to a failure in the DISTILLATE train, specifically a distillate pump trip. Alarms show P202_TRIP. This is consistent with a pump outage causing downstream pressure/temperature signatures and control loop compensation upstream.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong temperature and pressure excursions and multiple alarms. The strongest evidence points to an actuator fault affecting heating, with secondary evidence suggesting pressure control issues consistent with a stuck PCV or sensor bias.

PCA indicates large, coherent upset with strong high-temperature/pressure indications and an active temperature alarm. The most plausible causes point to a heater fault driving overheating, possibly with a concurrent sensor anomaly and/or catalyst-related upset.

A large, coherent plant upset with concurrent high reactor temperature alarms and a saturated temperature controller, consistent with an actuator fault on the CSTR heater driving excessive temperature.

PCA abnormal with strong coherent upset focused on reactor temperature and control loop; high reactor temperature alarm with a saturated R_TIC loop and SIF latched. Most likely a stuck/high reactor heater causing elevated temperature and triggering the alarm, with catalyst activity loss as a secondary contributor.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong high-temperature alarms in the CSTR. The dominant contributor is the reactor temperature rise driven by the heater path. The most likely faults are heater-related (actuator) issues causing excessive/unstable heating and possible temperature sensor corroboration.

The PCA monitor flags a strong, coherent upset with large T² and significant SPE, dominated by the reactor pressure signal. The most likely faults are H2 PCV issues causing abnormal reactor pressure response, with sensor bias also plausible.

The PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with both T² and SPE violations, with the CSTR pressure rising and the pressure sensor contributing strongly to the SPE. The most probable causes are related to H2 PCV faults causing limited venting and/or sensor bias at the reactor pressure measurement, consistent with PCV degradation/stuck condition and biased pressure reading.

High-dimension PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset dominated by reactor pressure measurement related variables, with the strongest contribution from CSTR pressure. The fault catalogue suggests H2 PCV issues (capacity degradation or stuck), consistent with a PCV-command/actual mismatch and reactor pressure anomalies.

PCA flags a large coherent upset with pronounced pressure and temperature disturbances centered on the CSTR. The strongest fault candidates from the catalogue point to H2 PCV issues causing reactor-pressure/vent-mismatch behavior.
Abnormal PCA with large coherent upset, dominated by reactor pressure increase with correlated temperature rise and PCV-related indicators; likely H2 PCV (vent) fault causing pressure build-up.

PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with both T² and SPE violations. Most consistent with an up-front tasking fault on the CSTR heater driving temperature up, with supporting hints of H2 PCV issues contributing to elevated reactor pressure.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with abnormal correlations (high T² and high SPE). The strongest evidence points to abnormal CSTR heating behavior driving the reactor temperature high relative to setpoints, consistent with a heater fault misbehaving.

The PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with both T² and SPE violated, with the SPE dominated by the op.R_TIC contribution. The rule-based hints point to a sensor fault on the R_TIC loop output rather than a pure process upset, suggesting a sensor/measurement issue affecting the TIC control signal.

The PCA shows a large, coherent upset with very high T² and SPE, driven predominantly by the CSTR temperature and the R_TIC loop signal. The most plausible causes are a sensor fault on op.R_TIC, or an actuator fault causing the reactor heater to behave abnormally, with catalyst activity loss as a less likely secondary contributor.

PCA detects a large, coherent upset dominated by CSTR temperature with high T² and high SPE, pointing to an actuator fault in the CSTR heater as the primary cause, with catalyst activity loss as a secondary possibility.

A large coherent process upset with both T² and SPE violations, with the strongest evidence pointing to a faulty reactor temperature control signal (op.R_TIC) causing the SPE. The temperature rise and controller action suggest a heating/heater-related issue or sensor fault propagating through the reactor control loop.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong SPE; the strongest evidence points to a sensor fault on the TIC temperature transmitter (op.R_TIC) driving the apparent anomaly. Other plausible causes include heater issues and catalyst-related effects, but op.R_TIC is the most consistent with the evidence.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations. Highest influence from reactor temperature with a notable heater-related mismatch signal suggests a heater-related fault is driving the upset.

The PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with both T2 and SPE violated. The leading contributors point to a CSTR temperature rise dominated by the reactor heating path, with sensor data largely contributing to the SPE. The most likely faults are related to the reactor heater path and catalyst/reaction-rate effects.

PCA flag indicates a large, coherent process upset with strong reactor temperature rise driving high T² and high SPE; most consistent with an abnormal CSTR heater behavior causing elevated reactor temperature and related feed/pressure responses.
Very large coherent process upset with reactor temperature rising and strong contribution from CSTR temperature; likely an actuator fault affecting heat input.

The PCA monitor shows a large, coherent process upset with both T2 and SPE violated, with the strongest rule-based indication pointing to a heater-related fault in the CSTR reactor. The most plausible single fault is reactor_heater_stuck_high, with catalyst_activity_loss as a secondary possibility.
